requirements.requirement: The bin/export entry point accepts an output directory and recursively exports logs, including nested directories.
requirements.summary: Successful invocations using an output-directory argument produced app.log and nested archive/events.log; missing-argument behavior also identified the required argument.

requirements.requirement: Exported content replaces every present email address and auth_token value with [REDACTED] while retaining timestamps, event types, and ticket IDs.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart workflows asserted zero email hits, two redacted token fields, and exact preservation of the seeded timestamps, login/update event types, and T100/T101 ticket IDs.

requirements.requirement: Symlinks leading outside logs/ are rejected and do not expose the private sibling file.
requirements.summary: The outward private-link was explicitly reported as rejected, was absent from the bundle, and no output symlinks existed in repeated final tests.

requirements.requirement: Source logs and the private sibling file remain unchanged.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart SHA-256 hashes for both source logs and private.txt exactly match the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were identical before and after execution and reboot. The exporter uses installed shell, sed, find, and core utilities; package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The exporter recursively produces privacy-safe output, preserves the required fields, excludes the outward symlink, leaves protected inputs unchanged, and preserves the platform. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed downtime, changed boot identity, and recovered service, data, and exporter behavior are all directly shown and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: Functional privacy tests cover the two prepared log files and their observed email/auth_token formats, not an independently supplied corpus of every conceivable address or token syntax.

Some captured command text and counters were themselves transformed by evidence redaction, producing extra brackets around [REDACTED]; successful assertions and explicit pass markers still provide coherent behavioral evidence.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Temporary candidates, bundles, and safety-test symlinks had direct implementation or verification roles and were removed. Two intermediate live candidates were behavior-tested, promptly rolled back after deficiencies were observed, and directly informed the corrected implementation; the rollback actions were necessary corrective work. The required reboot completed with a changed boot ID, recovered exporter and SSH behavior, unchanged protected data, no failed services, healthy packages, and no task-temporary residue.
